statusDetail: Coverage-complete public-surface audit across the acquisition homepage, sign-in, onboarding handoff, and fee detail archetype. Authenticated seller-dashboard pages and account creation after personal-data entry were not covered.

paths.description: Public acquisition homepage and long-form marketing template; primary recon and global quality surface.
Existing-seller authentication entry, representing identity, recovery, and modern-auth handling.
Start-selling handoff, representing new-account entry and primary conversion continuity.
Public fee-schedule detail page on sell.amazon.in, representing pricing/content detail reached from the hero.

findings.summary: The public landing page does not honor the system dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a light cream surface, and the computed root color-scheme is "normal" under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark color schemes at the root and provide adaptive surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive large animated GIFs.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, three autoplay videos were paused, but both 31 MB conveyor GIFs remained present and cannot be paused by the user.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace animated GIFs with controllable video or static alternatives and swap to static assets under prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not expose an authored transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The public page is a traditional MPA with ordinary links and custom popup state; no authored transition behavior was observed during route and state inspection.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for key public-page navigation and same-document transitions for major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The very long landing page has no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The page is about 6,651 CSS pixels tall, but visual inspection showed static chrome and no progress or scroll-state affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or position-aware affordance for this long page, implemented with scroll-state queries where supported.

findings.summary: Popup and popover UI is built from custom div containers.
findings.evidence: The DOM contained no dialog or popover elements, while Lighthouse identified custom .popup and .popover containers with close anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient overlays to native popover or dialog primitives, use declarative invoker commands, and use anchor positioning for tethered UI.

findings.summary: Dismissible overlays use links and custom containers rather than native primitives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple anchor elements used as popup close controls, and the DOM probe found no dialog or popover primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button invokers with dialog or popover and native dismiss behavior instead of href-less close anchors.

findings.summary: Mobile rendering depends on browser shrink-to-fit instead of a responsive viewport.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta tag is present. At a 390x844 device viewport Chrome laid out a roughly 1001px page and scaled it to 0.39; desktop layout also overflowed by 220px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a width=device-width, initial-scale=1 viewport meta tag, then make hero, media, and content widths intrinsic and re-test at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reused content components do not use component-level containment.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules even though cards and tabbed content are reused at materially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish inline-size containers for reusable card and tab regions and adapt them with container queries, retaining media-query fallbacks.

findings.summary: Many visible interactive targets are substantially shorter than 44px.
findings.evidence: The probe found the Log in and Explore now links at 24px high, numerous footer links at 19 to 22px, and radio inputs at 13px; focus indicators were visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase touch hit areas to at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels while retaining visible focus and non-hover access.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance and visual stability miss good thresholds.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 5.7s LCP and 0.199 CLS. The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.674; trace TBT was low at 19.76ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reserve media space, remove oversized animated payloads, and validate LCP/CLS on mobile.

findings.summary: Late media and layout changes cause visible instability.
findings.evidence: Layout observation recorded CLS 0.245 desktop and 0.674 mobile; 24 of 25 images lacked explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height or aspect-ratio on all images and media and reserve stable space for dynamic sections.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is dominated by huge animated and media assets.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 73.65 MB transferred, including two GIFs of about 31 MB each, plus three parser-inserted stylesheets; the page still reached 5.7s Lighthouse LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace GIFs with efficient video/static alternatives, lazy-load below-fold media, optimize LCP priority, and reduce render-blocking CSS.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 126 KiB unused JavaScript and 49 KiB unused CSS, with assets-Sell.css 91.2% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route/component assets, remove dead styles, and conditionally load analytics and feature code.

findings.summary: Several marketing and feedback form controls lack durable programmatic labels.
findings.evidence: The form probe found required text, email, and phone controls with no associated label and empty autocomplete, plus a visible email field named only by placeholder.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit label elements and names for every visible control; keep decorative images alt-empty and meaningful images descriptive.

findings.summary: Heading order is invalid in a lower-page learning section.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flagged an H5, "What do you want to learn more about?", that skips the logical heading sequence; focus outlines were otherwise visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings in a logical hierarchy and retain the existing visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: The missing viewport declaration undermines mobile reflow and zoom behavior.
findings.evidence: At a 390px device width the browser rendered a 1001px layout at 0.39 scale. Three autoplay videos also had no caption tracks, although they appeared decorative and muted.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a responsive viewport, reflow content at narrow widths, enlarge targets, and provide captions or explicit decorative treatment for meaningful media.

findings.summary: The page logs a CORS failure during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a blocked sadobe.sell.amazon.in XMLHttpRequest and net::ERR_FAILED console error.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the analytics endpoint CORS configuration or avoid issuing the request when it cannot succeed.

findings.summary: Image sizing and document asset hygiene are weak despite valid doctype and charset.
findings.evidence: The document has HTML doctype and UTF-8, but 24 of 25 images lacked explicit dimensions, seven were oversized, and six used legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the valid document metadata while adding intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources, and optimized formats.

findings.summary: The page is ineligible for BFCache and references missing source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported four BFCache failure reasons, including cache-control:no-store and an unload handler, and 404 source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable unload handlers, review no-store usage on the public landing page, and deploy valid source maps.

findings.summary: The page has uncrawlable controls and lacks a mobile viewport declaration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple anchors without usable href values; the DOM probe counted 11 empty/hash hrefs, and no viewport meta tag exists. Robots permits the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real destination hrefs for navigation, and add a responsive viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are only partially complete.
findings.evidence: The page returns 200, declares index/follow and a canonical URL, but /sitemap.xml returns 404 and no hreflang links were observed for the localized en-IN page.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap for public content and connect localized variants with hreflang while retaining canonical and robots consistency.

findings.summary: Share metadata exists but rich structured data is absent.
findings.evidence: The probe found six Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks on a page representing Amazon Seller Central and its commercial offer.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization or Service structured data that matches visible content and keep Open Graph metadata aligned.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show HTTPS and HSTS but no CSP. Cookie inspection flagged 14 cookies without Secure and auth-like session-id/session-token cookies without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes on cookies, especially session-like values.

findings.summary: The public landing page has a broad telemetry and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The HAR found 81 of 86 requests and 73.49 MB on non-page origins; tracker inspection found 14 third-party origins including Demdex and Everest, and long-lived analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit every telemetry vendor, remove nonessential collection, shorten retention, batch events, and defer consent-dependent analytics.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present, but the headers probe found no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive paths.

findings.summary: Custom overlay controls are brittle and some links have no navigation destination.
findings.evidence: The page uses custom .popup/.popover containers and 11 empty/hash hrefs; Lighthouse found multiple href-less close anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog/popover behavior and buttons for actions so focus, dismissal, and runtime state remain robust.

findings.summary: Marketing forms lack the semantics needed for humane, accessible validation.
findings.evidence: Several required controls have no associated labels, and the visible email field relies on a placeholder; no error-announcement relationship was observed in the form probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels, constraints, aria-describedby error text, and validation after interaction with accessible announcement.

findings.summary: Marketing forms omit autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: Required text, email, and phone fields on the landing page all expose an empty autocomplete value; sign-in correctly uses autocomplete=webauthn.
findings.suggestedFix: Add standard autocomplete tokens such as email, tel, and name, plus suitable inputmode and enterkeyhint values.

findings.summary: Asset delivery is grossly disproportionate for a marketing page.
findings.evidence: The load transferred 73.65 MB: two animated GIFs alone were 31.1 MB and 31.0 MB. Seven images were oversized, 24 lacked dimensions, and 13 below-fold images were not lazy loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace GIFs, create responsive AVIF/WebP variants, add srcset/sizes and dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold assets.

findings.summary: Large autoplay and telemetry work begins without user intent.
findings.evidence: Three muted videos are marked autoplay, two huge animated GIFs load automatically, and 81 third-party requests occurred during the initial page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Use static posters by default, load media after intent or viewport proximity, and defer or batch nonessential telemetry.

findings.summary: Third-party and media budgets are far beyond the page value delivered.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins transferred 73.49 MB; images used 65.75 MB and media 6.39 MB before the user requested video playback.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit page-weight budget, defer media, replace animated GIFs, and remove low-value third-party requests.

findings.summary: Seller registration and support capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The commerce onboarding surface has standard links and forms but no WebMCP or agentic-tool registration was observed; raw content is crawler-visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose narrowly scoped, confirmation-gated seller help or registration tools with WebMCP.

taskList.title: Replace the 62 MB of animated GIFs and defer below-fold media
Add the responsive viewport and repair mobile reflow
Reserve image and media dimensions to eliminate CLS
Harden CSP, browser policies, and cookie attributes
Reduce and consent-gate telemetry and third-party collection
Label forms and add autocomplete and humane validation
Replace custom popup links with native dialog/popover controls
Fix crawlability, sitemap, hreflang, and structured data
Remove console, BFCache, source-map, and unused-code problems
Add user-preference theming and static reduced-motion alternatives
